notes.title: Turnover Updated: v1.0.879
notes.content:
Turnover has been updated to v1.0.879.

[h1]v1.0.879 Changelog[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]New:[/b] Added menu identifiers in the lower right of the screen so you know where you are when navigating the menus.
[*][b]Changed/All:[/b] Significant rendering and CPU performance improvements. Should be be most impactful to those with low end systems.
[*][b]Changed/All:[/b] For non-Xinput controllers, DirectInput is now internally preferred over WinMM. This should reduce or even eliminate any controller related crashes, as well as fix issues with some controller triggers not working correctly.
[*][b]Changed/All:[/b] Improved rendering of vision cones.
[*][b]Changed/All:[/b] Better fallback in the case of a missing game resource.
[*][b]Changed/All:[/b] When an error is written to log.txt, the error message is also sent to standard output.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an uncommon case where the Shock Tropper would become temporarily stuck to the player when attacking.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an issue where the Shock Trooper would not turn correctly before attacking.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed F1 taking a screenshot when the game window was out of focus.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a tiny memory leak.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Other misc. fixes.
[/list]

notes.title: Turnover Updated: Borderless Full Screen Mode
notes.content:
Turnover has been updated to v1.0.865. 

This update adds a [b]Borderless[/b] option in the [b]Fullscreen[/b] setting in the [b]Options[/b] screen.

Borderless full screen is a windowed mode where the window is resized to cover the entire desktop and all "window dressing' is removed. It plays nicer with alt-tabbing, multi-monitor setups, or other situations where the normal full screen mode may have issues.

To try it out, go to the [b]Options[/b] Screen, and change the [b]Fullscreen[/b] setting to [b]Borderless[/b]. Your desktop resolution will automatically be selected.

[b]Note[/b]: Borderless full screen mode is only available for your desktop resolution. 
[list]
[*][b]New:[/b] Added a Borderless Full Screen option. This option is only available for your desktop resolution
[*][b]Fixed:[/b] Fixed a minor performance issue with level loading.
[*][b]Fixed:[/b] Fixed a minor performance issue with game rendering.
[/list]

notes.title: Turnover Updated: New Graphics Setting & Bug Fixes
notes.content:
Turnover has been updated to v1.0.858. This update revamps the render quality setting and fixes a few bugs.

[h1]Render Quality Setting[/h1]

The render quality setting has been changed to three choices:
[list]
[*] [b]Half Resolution:[/b] The game will be rendered at half the window resolution and will be scaled up to match the window resolution. This setting will reduce video RAM usage at an image quality loss. This can be useful if you are running a very old video card or an old on-board video chipset and need to increase performance.
[*] [b]1:1 Resolution:[/b]  The game will be rendered at the same resolution as the window resolution. This is considered the standard setting.
[*] [b]Double Resolution:[/b] The game will be rendered at double the window resolution, then scaled down to match the window resolution. This will consume more video RAM and require more processing power, but will give the best image quality.
[/list]

Here is an example of the quality differences:

[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10312364/9a5e0fcd5490c8f45f20113377e55817eff81243.png][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10312364/1809e41cd7b6184452b55b3dcac1ba67c83d2d8e.png[/img][/url]
[b]1920x1080 at Half Resolution[/b]

[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10312364/cf5de9abba1bbcd803c0956ba22a168ff5a4a994.png][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10312364/1f294eeee7390ba0df722620cb9b55c19cd1936f.png[/img][/url]
[b]1920x1080 at 1:1 Resolution[/b]

[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10312364/8fce6ffb189c26b08827c8565f3be1391a9e887a.png][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/10312364/e6ef45226169f824a705d611dfe773d914cc5786.png[/img][/url]
[b]1920x1080 at Double Resolution[/b]

[h1]Full Changelog[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Changed/All:[/b] Changed "Render Quality" in Options to "Render Resolution". Half Display Resolution, 1:1 Display Resolution, and Double Display Resolution are the new choices for game render quality.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a text alignment issue with the Save Slot selection dialog.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a couple of tiny memory leaks.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Minor performance optimizations.
[/list]

notes.title: Turnover Updated: Balances, bug fixes, and more.
notes.content:
Turnover has been updated to v1.0.848.

[h1]Notable Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*] In Windows, Visual C++ 2017 Redistributables are recommended. They will install the next time you launch Turnover.
[*] The internal framerate cap has been raised to 240. Turnover should now play nicer at high refresh rates.
[*] I've increased the internal rendering resolution of the game. Both low quality and ideal quality settings are affected. If you are running a very, very old system/laptop, the low quality setting is recommended.
[*] A handful of levels have been rebalanced to improve gameplay.
[/list]
[h1]Full Changelog[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]New:[/b] Launch Option: unlockcutscenes. Unlocks all cutscenes for viewing.
[*][b]Changed/Windows:[/b] Turnover has been compiled with VS2017. Visual C++ 2017 redistributables should be installed prior to first run.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Rewrote the resource loading system. This will improve memory usage and may fix some rare instances where sprites and sounds will fail to load.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Increased frame rate cap to 240. If you encounter tearing or stuttering, VSync is recommended.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Increased the internal rendering resolution. This should improve visual fidelity.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Unlocking the "More Stamina" perk now immediately fills the player's stamina meter.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Rebalanced some areas in a few levels.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Minor changes and clarifications to some cutscene dialog and text.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Minor UI changes.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an issue where portions of vision cones would sometimes be cut off when looking around.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an issue where all of  the player's stamina would not be available at the beginning of a level when the "More Stamina" perk is unlocked.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a few sprite issues.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a couple of incorrect error messages.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an instance where a missing resource error would not exit the game properly.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Performance optimizations.
[/list]

notes.title: Turnover: One Year Later
notes.content:
Turnover was released nearly a year ago on Dec. 15th, 2015.

Boy, time flies.

When I was preparing to release Turnover a year ago, I made a commitment to regularly update Turnover with fixes and features. Looking back, I have pushed about 10 notable updates to the game since it has been released. Considering I’m one guy, that’s not too bad.

I have been committed to updating Turnover and wanted to go back and take a look at some of the updates over the year.

[h1][b]01/07/2016 (First Post Release Update, v1.0.691)[/b][/h1]

http://steamcommunity.com/games/372250/announcements/detail/85932744224247060

This first update started addressing some controller issues, such as aim sensitivity. Admittedly, I’m not much of a controller player (at this point, at least), so over the course of the year, Turnover ended up seeing a lot of controller improvement updates.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/2ep5vmX.gif[/img]

[i]v1.0.691: An alert desaturation effect was added to give an additional visual hint to the enemy alert status.[/i]

[h1][b]02/22/2016 (First Major Update, v1.0.740)[/b][/h1]

http://steamcommunity.com/games/372250/announcements/detail/666901094067672576

This was Turnover’s first major update and marked a large, progressive improvement to the game.

Highlights:

[list]
    [*]Difficulty Modes: Easy, Normal, and Hard. This was to help address the difficulty for a number of players. Some players found the game a little too difficult and wanted a more forgiving experience. This was a very reasonable request.
   [*] Improved AI. I ended up rewriting a number of AI routines to fix issues and improve their actions.
    [*]Added the Security Server hacking mechanic.
   [*] Snap pickup throwing. Aiming to throw was no longer required, but snap throwing was less accurate.
   [*] New player collision, which allowed player to easily glide off walls.
   [*] Major aesthetic changes to the HUD, menus.
[/list]

I think this was Turnover’s most important update, since it added and improved so much. At this point, I felt that the core game was finished and I could move onto fixing issues and building on top of the game.

If something came up and I was unable to work on Turnover any longer, I would have been proud with how it turned out.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/rSDrQuNl.png[/img]

[i]v1.0.740: New difficulty modes were added to Turnover to address concerns about how challenging the game was. The difficulty modes ended up being renamed in a later update.[/i]

[h1][b]04/19/2016 015 (v1.0.755)[/b][/h1]

http://steamcommunity.com/games/372250/announcements/detail/622996262209550282

This update in April addressed important refund and review feedback. A significant addition was the extra health given to the player for easy mode. This update also fixed some concerns regarding followers, making them a little easier to work with.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/azXQBos.gif[/img]

[i]v1.0.755: One extra health was given to the player for easy mode, balancing it further.[/i]

[h1][b]06/14/2016 (Second Major Update, v1.0.784)[/b][/h1]

http://steamcommunity.com/games/372250/announcements/detail/611740042620218450

I might hesitate to call this update “major”, but I will because it added a requested feature: an in-game tutorial.

I developed Turnover to introduce new features, new enemies, and new gameplay situations slowly over the course of the entire game, so you are always experiencing something new and are eased slowly into the game. You don’t really get to do everything in the game until you are about half way through. By that time, you’ll be more equipped to handle the more challenging second half of the game.

I always felt that Turnover was paced well. You are introduced to a new feature of the game in a level, then that feature becomes integrated throughout the rest of the game. I didn’t want to throw players into the deep end. Regardless, a tutorial was implemented, just to get the players’ feet wet before they dove in.

This update also brought a rewrite of the enemy hearing system. This was a major backend improvement. The original version “worked”, but was prone to quirkiness. This rewrite busted every outstanding enemy alert bug I had logged.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/HFq6m1n.png][img]http://i.imgur.com/HFq6m1nl.png[/img][/url]

[i]v1.0.784: An in game tutorial was added to give new players a hand at the fundamentals of the game.[/i]

[h1][b]07/26/2016 (Custom Level Support Update, v1.0.795)[/b][/h1]

http://steamcommunity.com/games/372250/announcements/detail/609493948031680013

This update added a feature that was requested in Turnover’s Steam discussion forum: custom level support. When I started making it work, I had thought it would be difficult to implement, but it ended up being relatively easy.

This update was just a fun update. It also gave me an excuse to get some bug fixes live.

[url=http://i.imgur.com/xI8Ka8m.png][img]http://i.imgur.com/xI8Ka8ml.png[/img][/url]

[i]v1.0.795: Custom level support was added, allowing users to create levels using Tiled Map Editor. Documentation was also included.[/i]

[h1][b]09/20/2016 (Controller Improvement Update, v1.0.804)[/b][/h1]

http://steamcommunity.com/games/372250/announcements/detail/597114129690756956

I started working on this update after taking a month off from Turnover, and then playing through it again with a new controller. So, this update revolves around controller improvements and fixing things I encountered during the new play through.

For the controller, I pushed a change where aiming makes better use of analog values, so aiming with analog sticks is far more precise. Also, I added the ability to select which controller you would like to use in the Option Menu if you have multiple controllers plugged in.

Outside of that, I addressed a number of things I ran into during my new play session. I improved Security Cameras, balanced a few levels, fixed some art quirks, and took care of other misc. issues.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/8wkifhi.gif[/img]

[i]v1.0.804: Analog stick aiming was improved, taking analog values more appropriately into account.[/i]

[h1][b]11/22/2016 (Save Slots, Steam Cloud and XInput Support, v1.0.832)[/b][/h1]

http://steamcommunity.com/games/372250/announcements/detail/522809610148221589

This update came from things I just felt should be added to the game. I wanted to create a big update to cap off Turnover’s first year of release. So, this update addressed many outstanding bugs in my issue tracker, and also added some features purely just to please me and to build upon the game.

One major addition in this update is save slots. For full disclosure, this was suggested to me by my lead tester very early in development. It had remained in my todo list until I had run through everything else that was of higher priority.

Since I was messing with saves, it felt like the right time to add Steam Cloud support. With cloud saves, I was able to check off the last of Valve’s recommended Steamworks features.

This update also added XInput support in Windows. Having recently been playing with an XBox One controller, I felt that the controller setup in Turnover was not tuned well for these. Turnover didn’t have any of the input contexts or vibration niceties that many players come to expect with robust Xbox controller support. Since XBox controllers are very popular, I felt that fully supporting them through XInput (with force feedback) was ultimately the right thing to do. Taking care of this basically put Turnover controller support into a finished state.

While adding XInput in, I realized the existing text-based input context hints were not cutting it  any longer, so I changed all input contexts to graphic icons. Now KB/M and Xbox controllers have their own custom icons. Generic controllers are using generic controller icons.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/wvUfQ3q.gif[/img]

[i]v1.0.832: XInput was utilized to give proper, full Xbox controller support (with rumble) in Windows. In addition, new input context icons were added.[/i]

[h1][b]In 2017[/b][/h1]

So, what’s the status of Turnover right now? Well, it’s at a state where I am very proud of it. My todo list, issue tracker, everything related to it, is empty. For all intents and purposes, it’s done.

Looking back on the game put me in a weird place. The amount of man hours I have put into it is pretty staggering, but I don’t regret one second of the work. I have learned so much and have developed a tremendous amount of skills during Turnover’s development. Personally, to me, the game is a resounding success and a landmark in my personal development.

So, what’s in store for Turnover in 2017? If people are still interested, and I find new and creative things to add to the game, and I have no major disruptions in my life, then I’ll continue to update it.

Until then, I’m off to work on my next game.

notes.title: Turnover Updated: Controller Improvements & More
notes.content:
Turnover has been updated to v1.0.804, bringing general improvements to the game.

[h1]Controllers[/h1]
[list]
[*] Controller aiming now makes better use of analog values, increasing aiming accuracy. Controller users who have an analog stick are now encouraged to bind move/aim to an analog stick if possible.
[*] If you have multiple controllers plugged into your PC, you can now select which one you would like to use from the Options menu.
[/list]
[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
[list]
[*] Security Cameras will now throw a general "suspicious" alert if a camera check is triggered multiple times within a short period.
[*] A few sections in some later levels have been rebalanced. This is to ensure a more consistent difficulty ramp as the game progresses. More or less, these levels will now be slightly easier.
[/list]
[h1]Full Changelog[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]New:[/b] Controller selection now available in Options menu if multiple controllers are plugged into the PC. Note: If controller is set to "Disabled" in Options, Universal Input (for menus) will use the default/preferred controller of the OS if one is plugged in.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Controller/Aiming: Axis binds now utilize range (analog) values for aiming, increasing fine touch and accuracy when using analog sticks.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Binds Menu: Changed "Aim Sensitivity" to "Controller Aim Speed".
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemy/All: Enemies that are killed will now dim in color.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemy/Security Turret: Slightly increased the delay between spotting and firing.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemy/Security Turret: When spotting/ranging, a Turret's vision cone will turn red, even before firing.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemy/Security Camera: If something(s) triggers a camera check 3 times within a 5 second period, the camera will become suspicious and will throw an alert.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Pickups: A "denial" sound will play if the player tries to pick up an object of the same type that they are already holding.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Music: Added some music to the transition between levels.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Cutscene: Slightly changed the transition between the final levels to warn of upcoming bosses.

[*][b]Fixed/Linux:[/b] Fixed a small memory leak.
[*][b]Fixed/Linux:[/b] Fixed the window icon not being displayed in some distros.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] On game launch, the default mouse cursor will be moved to a position away from menu elements to prevent accidental selection when using a controller.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a rare issue with the name of the current world not being displayed on the main menu if a game is in progress.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] In Options, stopped the selection blip sound from playing when trying to increase HUD Opacity past 100%.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] In Options, fixed the Volume selection preview sound not playing when selecting the 100% value.

[h1]Major Updates[/h1]

[list]
[*][b]New difficult modes: Hostage (easy), Survivor (normal), and Specialist (hard). Game has been balanced in favor of slightly more cover, improved mechanics, and better AI.[/b]

[*][b]AI Improvements and new AI states: More cautious and better AI. Enemies prefer turn-to-look as opposed to snap-looking. Enemies pay better attention to threats.[/b]
[*][b]Ability to throw objects without aiming (with penalty).[/b]
[*][b]Bug fixes and much more![/b]

[*][b]New:[/b] Security Server: New gameplay mechanic: password input. To disable a server, the player must enter a simple password sequence.
[*][b]New:[/b] Sentinel: New gameplay mechanic: suspicion. Certain noises and spotted projectiles will make Sentinels take a slower, more cautious approach to checking out the source.
[*][b]New:[/b] Player: Will slide across walls when moving. Remedies corner/collision sticking.
[*][b]New:[/b] Player: Can throw/use pickup objects without aiming, but doing so will incur a heavy accuracy penalty.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Hard Mode was changed to Specialist mode. No longer needs to be unlocked.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Survivor/Specialist Difficulty: Levels: Balanced levels, adding a little more cover at parts.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Survivor/Specialist Difficulty: Sentinel: Pistol bullet speed reduced by ~30%.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Survivor/Specialist Difficulty: Sentinel: Burst pistol bullet speed reduced by ~28%.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Survivor/Specialist Difficulty: Shock Trooper: Slightly reduced benefit of the Slow Reactions perk.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Survivor/Specialist Difficulty: Reduced fire's stamina drain rate.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemies/NPCs: New path walking routine, resulting in smoother paths and eliminating movement hitching.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Sentinel: Improved AI when spotting, hearing, and searching for suspicious activity.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Sentinel: Slightly easier to distract with noise.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Sentinel/Shock Trooper/Fireman: Removed most instances of snap spotting in favor of turning to spot.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Fireman: Fireman now explodes on grenade hit, instead of malfunctioning.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Sergeant: Vision cone is slightly shorter.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Security Server: New interaction, Press "Use" to disable, hold "Use" to preview what the server is controlling.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Security Server/Security Camera: Alerted Sentinels now have less of a chance to stack on top of each other when they are checking out an alert situation.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemies/Player: Colored outline changed to a black pop out.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemies: Improved enemy corner-spotting variance. Enemies will have worse vision the farther away you are, giving the player a tiny bit of leeway.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Enemies: Improved enemy attention. Enemies will now more often ignore other threats/attention getters when spotting the player and NPCs.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Throwables: Certain throwables now lose velocity as they travel.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Pickups: Increased standard delay between pickups.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Effects: Added animation to Fire Extinguisher and Flame Thrower spray sprites.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Perks: Clarified perk level hints.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Levels: Added missing shadows to some deco, removed unusual shadows from other deco.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Binds: The "Dismiss" bind has been removed. All major game interactions are now handled by the "Interact" & "Use" binds.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Game Camera: The Sprint" bind now skips camera/node previews. A HUD Hint was added to inform the player.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] Pause Screen: Restyled, fixed positioning and other issues, removed the help hints, added a little more color. Now relays more info to the player as well.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] HUD: Ammo indicator now uses color (green->red) to indicate ammo.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] HUD: Certain text and hints have been given text shadows.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] HUD: More context hints for workers and servers.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] HUD: Menu key hints made stylistically similar and moved to hint area.
[*][b]Changed:[/b] HUD: Hide mouse cursor during cutscenes.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an issue with the Sentinel's stun time sometimes being way too short.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed some rare instances where enemies wouldn't investigate noise generated from thrown objects.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed water and enemy blood clipping into walls on generation.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Reduced length of stun stars effect when someone was stunned. Initially played for too long.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an issue with the Security Camera's hitbox being too large.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed the Attack Dog's vision cone turning to yellow warning while attacking player.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Tightened Security Server HitBox to prevent warping when attempting to deactivate when not directly at the keyboard.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed incorrect Fire Extinguisher hitbox.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Added some missing footstep sounds when Worker is walking, as well as typing sounds when they deactivate a server.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an issue where NPCs could not be called when player is butting up against certain walls.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed vision cones sometimes drawing through walls.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a small issue where vision cone detection area would be slightly larger than what is drawn.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed light flicker not working at low frame rates.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a few instances in levels where enemies can spot you at the very entrance of a level.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a few times where enemies would take incorrect patrol paths.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed various timing issues.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed numerous projectile collision issues.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed pickups and dispensers conflicting when player collides with both.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed HUD Hints sometimes overlaying over certain entities, blocking their view.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed certain cutscenes not unlocking correctly for Theater.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a few sprite issues.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Screen shake was not being applied equally to all render textures, causing some weird looking results.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a couple of game over screen game hints being cut off on low resolutions.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a "Failed to open sound file from memory (format not supported)" warning message when running from the console/terminal in some levels.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed startup check when game fails to launch because of a system incompatibility or renderer initialization failure. It should now report your problem to log.txt so you know what's going on.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a startup crash issue with font handling.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed an intermittent crash while loading screens/levels.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Fixed a couple of tiny memory leaks.
[*][b]Fixed/All:[/b] Performance optimizations.
[/list]

notes.title: Turnover: Updated to v.1.0.691, Controller Improvements and Misc. Fixes.
notes.content:
Turnover's first post release update is now live! v1.0.691 improves controller support, brings some stylistic additions, and addresses bugs.

[h1]Aim Sensitivity[/h1]

For controller users, there is a new Aim Sensitivity option that sets the speed of aiming/looking ahead. The option can be found in the Binds menu.

[h1]Controller Menu Navigation Fix: New Launch Option[/h1]

I've had a couple of reports that some controllers clash with the default binds, making menu navigation difficult. To help players with this problem, there is now a new launch option: [b]setcontroller[/b]. Running this option will take you straight to the Binds screen, where you can easily set the correct binds so you can navigate the menus and play the game.

[h1]Binds Menu Access[/h1]

Access to the Binds menu from the title screen has been moved to the Options menu, just to keep things grouped together. Also, you can now access the Binds menu from the Pause screen, for easier checking or changing while in-game.

[h1]v1.0.691 Changelog[/h1]

[list]
[*]New: Controller aim sensitivity is now configurable from the Binds screen.
[*]New: The Binds screen can be accessed from the Pause screen for quick changing/reference.
[*]New: New launch options: setkbm and setcontroller. These take you straight to the Binds screen so you can set your binds down the line. Useful if you controller isn't compatible with the default binds, causing menu navigation issues.
[*]New: Sergeant alerts will now trigger the minimap alert indicator.
[*]New: Alerting patrols/Sergeants will trigger a color desaturation effect. Colors return when patrols are no longer alerted.
[*]Changed: Access to the Binds screen has been moved to the Options screen.
[*]Changed: "Pause" will no longer skip the server preview and level opening. "Use" and "interact" still do.
[*]Changed: Reworded some HUD text for clarity.
[*]Changed: Slightly increased the camera preview pause between nodes.
[*]Changed: Slightly better fallback if the game's config file is corrupt/malformed.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed a HUD warning on the Binds Screen if a bind is not set.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed the camera flying to the wrong place if the game is paused during the server preview/opening camera preview.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed an intermittent issue with the camera missing the first preview spot on level start.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed female workers sometimes not being assigned first names for their ID cards.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed a few incorrectly worded error messages if a log file is generated.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta Build Updated: Build 637
notes.content:
Turnover has been updated to beta build 637. This build adds some atmospheric things and addresses a number of issues.

[h1]Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*]New: Added some atmospheric light fixture flickering throughout some levels.
[*]New: Added lighting effects to fire.
[*]New: More sounds / sound variety added to enemies. Ensured each enemy has individual "voices", as well as event sounds.
[*]New: Security Turret: Added detection light: white on watch, yellow on focus, red on spotted.
[*]New: Added a tiny visual indicator on noise objects when they are stepped on.
[*]New: Added more log file outputs to track down bugs.
[*]Changed: Changed the reticle style.
[*]Changed: Modified a couple of HUD colors.
[*]Changed: Better shading variance on fire extinguisher spray.
[*]Changed: Security Camera: Detection light modified: white on watch, yellow on focus, red on spotted.
[*]Changed: Increased max number of spawnable fire/effects entities. Should fix any problems with disappearing fire.
[*]Changed: Improved minimum resolution requirement check.
[*]Changed: Improved valid resolution check, specifically for full screen usage.
[*]Changed: If only one full screen resolution is detected, give player some windowed modes to select.
[*]Fixed/All: Clea's death animation failed to play after getting shot while being mauled by an Attack Dog.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed a couple of small cases where collision between the world & the player would be incorrectly evaluated.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed an issue where fire would sometimes not destroy Security Cameras.
[*]Fixed/All: Modified how resolution changes are handled. Should be safer & have less potential to crash with iffy drivers/cards.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed an issue with sound initialization.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed an issue with sound spatialization when aiming.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed a potential memory leak.
[*]Fixed/All: Minor optimizations.
[/list]

notes.title: Beta Build Updated: Build 628
notes.content:
Turnover has been updated to build 628 for beta testers. This is mostly an optimization update.

[h1]Changes:[/h1]

[list]
[*]Changed: Minor optimization by reducing the frequency of some Steam feature checks.
[*]Changed: New NPC vision cone rendering method, resulting in more accurate draw checks and a performance improvement.
[*]Changed: Added a few new log outputs for errors.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed an issue where attempting to drag the window while the Steam Overlay was open would cause the game to freeze.
[*]Fixed/All: Fixed a couple of potential memory leaks.
[*]Fixed/All: Some minor performance & memory optimizations.
[*]Fixed/All: (Included in previous hotfix) Fixed the inability to complete level 4.
[*]Fixed/OS X: Improved memory management.
[/list]
